text:
maria: Quick heads up — saw a staging worker startup log that contains a truncated API key fragment. Not sure if it was uploaded to our logs bucket. Can someone from infra/security advise next steps? :eyes:

security-bot: :rotating_light: Automated secret scanner flagged: detected pattern resembling API key in /var/log/worker/startup.log (staging). Alert ID: 4321. No full key matched, only a 24-char base64 fragment.

jason: Can you paste the exact log line (redact fully if necessary)? We need to know if it was just printed or actually written to object storage.

maria: here — redacted partial: `2026-03-16T04:12:07Z worker[pid=322]: service init, API_KEY=eyJhbGciOiJIU...<trunc>...k3L`

olivia: That looks like a truncated token printed by the docker entrypoint. Which image version? If it's only local container stdout that's different than S3.

maria: staging image tag `staging-2026.03.11-build7`. I grepped s3 prefix quickly and saw the file uploaded `s3://redwood-logging/staging/2026-03-16/worker-322.log` — it contains the same line.

infra-oncall: Ok — steps: 1) rotate the exposed credential if it's still valid (emergency rotation). 2) redact the uploaded log object (or delete and re-ingest cleaned copy). 3) run scanner across yesterday's uploads for similar patterns. Who can rotate the key?

devops: I can rotate if we know which key (service account vs user API key). Maria — which credential did the container use? Env var name suggests service token used by bootstrap script.

maria: It's the deployer service token (SERVICE_BOOTSTRAP_KEY). It should be short-lived but not sure of TTL — probably created in Jan.

jason: If it's a Vault-wrapped token, we should revoke the Vault token and create a new one. If it's an external API key stored in KMS-wrapped secret, rotate at provider. Either way, follow emergency rotation runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/secret-rotation-emergency (ask for approval).

olivia: Paging @sam and @security-oncall group for approval to rotate and to redact logs. We need an approval note in the ticket for audit. :shield:

sam: approve — emergency rotation OK. Please file an incident ticket and include which artifacts you deleted/redacted.

devops: Commands I'll run (doing this now):
```
# list candidate logs
aws s3 ls s3://redwood-logging/staging/2026-03-16/ --recursive | grep worker-322
# copy, redact, and replace object
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-logging/staging/2026-03-16/worker-322.log ./worker-322.log
sed -E 's/(API_KEY=)[A-Za-z0-9_\-\.\=]+/\1<REDACTED>/g' worker-322.log > worker-322.redacted.log
aws s3 cp worker-322.redacted.log s3://redwood-logging/staging/2026-03-16/worker-322.log --acl bucket-owner-full-control
# rotate credential (example for Vault token)
vault token revoke s.TOKENID
# create new token and update secret in secret-manager
```

infra-oncall: Also run a `grep -E` scan across the bucket for base64-like strings longer than 20 chars and flag matches. I'll kick off a bucket-scan job and post results here.

security-bot: Scan started (job 9876). I'll post matches to the ticket when done. Reminder: for audit, include who approved rotation and who replaced the secret.

maria: I've created incident RED-2026-118 and added the initial findings + the redacted object. Will update after rotation and scan.

devops: Rotation done — revoked old token, created new service token, updated staging secret in Vault and redeployed workers. Replaced log object with redacted copy. Added notes to RED-2026-118.

sam: thanks. Two quick followups: 1) Add a CI check to fail builds that echo env vars on startup. 2) Shorten token TTL for bootstrap tokens to 24h max.

jason: I'll open a PR with a lint-rule for entrypoint scripts (deny printing secrets) + CI job. Will link to the incident.

maria: All good from my side. Thanks everyone for the fast turn. Closing once security-bot confirms no other matches. :white_check_mark:

security-bot: Scan complete — no other matches found in 48h window. Closing alert 4321.
